{{Current events|year=2020|month=01|day=6|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)]]
**The [[Libyan National Army]] says it has captured [[Sirte]] and the [[Ghardabiya Airbase|Al-Qardabiya airbase]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jan/06/libyan-general-khalifa-haftars-forces-seize-key-city-of-sirte (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2020 Gamboru bombing]]
**At least 30 people are killed in [[Gamboru]], [[Borno State]], in northeastern [[Nigeria]] after an [[improvised explosive device]] [[detonate]]s at a market on a bridge. No group immediately took responsibility. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-nigeria-security/thirty-killed-in-northeast-nigeria-bomb-blast-on-crowded-bridge-idUSKBN1Z526J (Reuters)]
*[[Mali War]]
**Five [[Malian Armed Forces|soldiers]] are killed after their vehicle hit a [[Improvised explosive device|roadside bomb]] while traveling in the [[Alatona]] region. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/01/malian-soldiers-killed-roadside-attack-200106143333076.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Funerals of Qasem Soleimani]]
**A funeral service for [[Qasem Soleimani]], the [[Iran|Iranian]] [[Quds Force]] commander who was slain in a [[2020 Baghdad International Airport airstrike|targeted killing in Baghdad last week]], is attended by hundreds of thousands of people in [[Tehran]], [[Iran]]. [https://www.npr.org/2020/01/06/794044616/iran-mourns-slain-gen-qassem-soleimani-and-vows-revenge (NPR)] [https://www.axios.com/qasem-soleimani-iran-funeral-photos-f83662b9-dce3-4a7c-9e92-e0a24843e8ba.html (Axios)]

;Business and economy
*American retailer [[Pier 1 Imports]] announces it will close 450 stores and some [[distribution center]]s, and may soon file for [[Bankruptcy in the United States|bankruptcy]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/01/06/business/pier-1-imports-bankruptcy/index.html (CNN)]

;Disasters and accidents
*A 5.8 magnitude [[earthquake]] strikes [[Puerto Rico]], causing small [[landslide]]s, [[power outage]]s, and severely cracking some homes. [https://nbc25news.com/news/nation-world/57-magnitude-quake-strikes-puerto-rico-damage-reported (Associated Press)]
*A [[Germans|German]] [[tourism in Italy|tourist]] critically wounded in the crash yesterday in [[Luttach]], [[Italy]], dies from her injuries, bringing the death toll to seven. [https://www.ilgazzettino.it/italia/primopiano/incidente_alto_adige_6_morti_ragazzi_chi_sono-4965506.html (Il Gazzettino)]

;Law and crime
*A court in the [[United Kingdom]] sentences 36-year-old [[Indonesians in the United Kingdom|Indonesian]]  national [[Reynhard Sinaga]] to [[life imprisonment]] for [[sexually assault]]ing at least 48 young men in [[Manchester]]. Sinaga was convicted of a total of 159 [[sex offence]]s, and is said to be Britain's most prolific [[serial rapist]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-50987823 (BBC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-britain-rapist/indonesian-student-jailed-as-britains-worst-rapist-idUSKBN1Z519D (Reuters)]
*[[Law enforcement in Germany|Police]] shoot dead a [[Turks in Germany|Turkish]] man who tried to attack officers with a knife in the city of [[Gelsenkirchen]], [[North Rhine-Westphalia]], [[Germany]]. Police say a search of the man's flat later did not suggest a [[terrorism in Germany|terrorist]] motive and that he was [[mentally ill]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-51003868 (BBC)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Politics of the Marshall Islands]]
**[[David Kabua]] is elected [[President of the Marshall Islands]] by the [[Legislature of the Marshall Islands|national legislature]]. He succeeds [[Hilda Heine]], who was seeking a second term, but lost in the first session vote. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/406763/new-president-for-marshall-islands (Radio New Zealand International)]
